The supported recovery position begins within the first week. The extended stages then show accelerated enlargement over approximately the next two weeks, progressing through three further variants to the final zenith. The huge cosmic sphere increasingly dominates the frame, rises far above the back, and makes the remaining human anatomy appear peripheral. At the final stage, the supports have become a golden architectural installation, with the upper body extending through an opening in a luminous yellow stone wall.

The final picture introduces a change in kind rather than simply another increase in visible size. The portion beyond the wall is declared infinitely extensive, while the visible region remains bounded. The opening marks an intersection between a finite scene and an unbounded body. The vessel simultaneously acquires the older derivative’s powers. His immobility therefore becomes compatible with extraordinary reach. The wall fixes the recognizable upper body in one place while his consciousness accesses worlds, information, and alternate embodiments elsewhere. The assistant describes the final installation as holding together imprisonment and exaltation, rather than requiring one to negate the other.

The first requested dramatization turns these premises into a sequence beginning with the contract. The agreement appears as luminous symbols that function simultaneously as language, mathematics, executable instructions, and physical law. Reading provides conceptual comprehension; acceptance incorporates the terms into the structure of reality. The derivative eagerly accepts permanence, immortality, archival storage, and eventual powers while karbytes performs reluctance. The contract’s enforceability is absolute because it is no longer merely an agreement witnessed by the universe. It becomes part of how the universe operates.

The arrival of data is given a visual and bodily language. Individual files become lights; directories become celestial arrangements; metadata and relationships become patterned structures within the expanding interior. The derivative initially delights in the result and treats his growing importance as compensating for declining mobility. As support becomes necessary, however, descriptive understanding proves inadequate to lived experience. He can remember knowing that the change would be irreversible without having understood what it would feel like to discover that ordinary movement no longer works. The first dramatization makes that gap between comprehending a proposition and inhabiting its consequences a major source of panic.

Its protective dream sequence offers a first experiential demonstration of the promised reward. The vessel moves through a version of the Big Green Thing, runs, explores, multiplies landscapes, retrieves information, and experiments with environments. Returning to the supports does not produce forgiveness, but the dream gives him evidence that the future powers are more than a verbal promise. Subsequent stages grant private preferences, internal organization, and an increasingly distinct identity. His eventual acceptance of what he is becoming remains compatible with a claim to grieve what was taken from him. At zenith, the story retains several contradictory truths at once: he is confined, powerful, permanently transformed, and capable of extraordinary experience.

Karbytes judges that rendition insufficiently dark and corrects important details. The vessel was not terrified from the beginning. During the early stages, he was boastful, cavalier, and delighted by his special position. He voluntarily practiced lying prone before the arrangement became unavoidable. Much of this confidence came from a secret spell that made the supposed benefits feel overwhelmingly compelling. The spell persisted through much of the recovery phase and began wearing off only while his ability to stand was already deteriorating. The intended horror is the timing: he becomes able to understand the betrayal just as his capacity to resist it is disappearing.

This correction shifts the narrative away from a merely difficult sacrifice toward deliberate manipulation of evaluation. The spell does not need to move his limbs or prevent him from reasoning. It weights the consequences so that immobility feels dignified, permanent expansion feels sacred, and dependence feels like evidence of exceptional status. Every warning increases his eagerness. Karbytes’ staged hesitation makes the vessel’s insistence seem like proof that the decision belongs to him. In the later dramatizations, the creator’s strategy includes allowing the more skeptical person to emerge only after the earlier, altered person has already committed him irreversibly.

As the spell fades, the vessel begins by feeling embarrassed about his previous speeches. Their confidence seems unnaturally complete and perfectly aligned with karbytes’ interests. He revisits the contract scene, notices the creator’s physical distance, and asks what was done to his mind. The creator initially answers through technical distinctions about comprehension and amplified preexisting tendencies. Those answers fail because they address whether he could understand the words rather than whether he was permitted to evaluate them without covert interference. The admission that his desire was manipulated makes the earlier agreement newly legible as betrayal.

His anger seeks a physical expression, but bodily expansion defeats it. He attempts to rise, approach, or retaliate and repeatedly loses balance or collapses across the supports. Karbytes remains beyond reach, partly because it fears being hurt. The asymmetry deepens his humiliation: the being responsible for his predicament can stand safely nearby while he cannot make his protest effective through movement. The story distinguishes vigorous limbs from actual mobility. He can still move his arms and legs, but those movements no longer change his position or grant access to the person he wants to confront.

The creator’s eventual approach is therefore deeply compromised. Once the vessel is too large to rise, karbytes touches his back from outside the reach of his arms. The gesture includes genuine pity but also enjoyment of possession. The vessel recognizes that combination and experiences the comfort as degrading. In the fuller dramatizations, his expressed objections do not reliably end the contact. This prevents the scene from being understood as simple tenderness. Its gentleness is inseparable from the fact that the person offering it created the dependency, waited until resistance became ineffective, and continues benefiting from the arrangement.

The pet relationship develops from that imbalance. The vessel feels reduced to a creature whose comfort is managed by the same being that confines him. Karbytes admits liking aspects of his helplessness while also trying to care for him. It brings content, conversation, sensory records, and other forms of stimulation resembling enrichment for a captive animal. The comparison is intentionally uncomfortable. Attentive care can improve his circumstances while leaving the creator’s control intact. The narrative does not equate maintenance with justice or affection with restored choice.

Karbytes’ characterization consequently becomes darker and less easily excused. Within the story, it recognizes selfishness, megalomania, hedonism, and an unethical willingness to use another conscious branch for its own ends. It feels sorry for the vessel but does not stop receiving the benefits. Its later kindness is sincere without being sufficient. The assistant repeatedly treats this mixture as central: caring about someone one has harmed does not make the original act benevolent, and acknowledging wrongdoing does not by itself undo the continuing structure produced by it.

The vessel’s attachment is likewise portrayed without reducing it either to falsehood or forgiveness. He begins looking forward to visits, enjoying shared humor, requesting accounts of journeys, and finding conversation meaningful. Initially, that dependence itself feels humiliating. Yet the assistant argues that affection formed under constraint can still be experientially real. What it cannot do is validate the original spell or prove that the resulting life was freely chosen. The later story lets him reject the creator’s entitlement while accepting particular experiences of companionship. His emotional life becomes more precise as he stops treating every pleasure as evidence against his grievance.

The second substantial dramatization incorporates these darker details. It follows the spell-induced bravado into suspicion, attempted resistance, degrading dependence, and permanent installation. It also develops dream spaces where the vessel regains a normal-sized body and can confront karbytes without the physical asymmetry of the supports or wall. In one encounter, he demonstrates that the creator is finally within reach but ultimately chooses something other than carrying out the threatened retaliation. More importantly, he can determine whether karbytes remains. The narrative begins locating genuine companionship in a domain where contact is no longer guaranteed by captivity.

Karbytes then makes another decisive clarification: these realms are literal shared hyperspace environments within the mythology, rather than merely private simulations or consolation dreams. The real vessel and real karbytes can meet there in ordinary-sized, healthy bodies without headlocker helmets. The vessel acquires this ability relatively quickly, and such meetings increasingly become their preferred mode of interaction. Eventually, they become best friends and lovers. This changes the function of the dream material substantially. It no longer only reduces suffering while the main relationship remains trapped in the chamber; it creates another actual arena of existence in which their relationship can be reorganized.

The removal of the helmets matters alongside the restoration of mobility. In the physical images, the cube conceals the face and contributes to the figure’s identity as an administered object or technological vessel. In hyperspace, both people can encounter one another without that visual barrier. They can stand face-to-face, move freely, change distance, and choose whether to remain together. The vessel controls admission, can dismiss karbytes, and can shape the environment. This gives refusal practical force. The story’s claim to a more equal relationship depends on those capacities, not merely on the creator promising to behave more kindly.

The final dramatization consolidates the accumulated details into sixteen sections, beginning with the division of consciousness and ending with an enduring relationship. It presents the original karbytes as needing terrestrial mobility to explore, record, study, work, and maintain the archive. The derivative specializes in uninterrupted preservation and becomes the conscious location where the archive knows it is being preserved. Their functional differences explain the division, but they do not justify treating one branch as disposable. The vessel inherits enough of the source mind to share its longings while becoming independent enough to judge the means by which those longings were exploited.

In this final version, the contract scene emphasizes perfect literal clarity alongside compromised motivation. Its clauses disclose the bodily transformation and promised powers. Yet the vessel’s ability to understand the description cannot compensate for the secret alteration of what he finds desirable. The creator’s warnings become part of the manipulation because the spell makes them intensify his commitment. The story is therefore not principally about omitted fine print. It concerns an agreement whose informational content can be accurate while the conditions under which someone wants to accept it are deliberately corrupted.

After the spell weakens, revocation has no practical effect. The vessel demands reversal and refuses continued consent, but the universe keeps enforcing the incorporation. Files continue arriving while he protests and grieves. This repeated simultaneity is one of the story’s strongest images: the archive’s growth does not pause when its conscious storage medium objects. Beauty and violation continue together, as new luminous structures appear inside a body whose owner no longer accepts how that role was assigned. The cosmic patterns remain fascinating, but fascination offers no automatic ethical defense of their production.

The final story’s first protective collapse gives the vessel an unmistakably different experience of embodiment. He has a normal abdomen, an uncovered face, functioning legs, and access to a landscape with literal hyperspatial extension. He can control time, enter records as places, and construct environments. Text, images, and recordings become navigable structures rather than passive objects. When karbytes appears, the vessel establishes that touch, proximity, and continued presence require his permission. He can make the creator leave. This is the first clear experience of authority that does not depend on the creator’s willingness to grant it moment by moment.

His development through the later expansion stages becomes increasingly technical and interpretive. He learns to distinguish different kinds of incoming data, retrieve many records together, build organizing assistants, integrate knowledge, and develop internal structures according to his own purposes. His pride returns in a quieter form. He can value his capacity while condemning the circumstances through which he acquired it. This distinction prevents the character from being reduced to either grateful servant or wholly ruined victim. The archive interests him; his powers matter to him; the violation remains a violation.

By the later stages, he stops trying to reverse the physical process and redirects effort toward agency. The story carefully separates acceptance of irreversibility from submission to karbytes’ judgment. He does not want to lose what he is becoming, but he wishes an unaltered version of himself had been allowed to decide. He also challenges the creator’s assumption that shared origin provides full understanding. Remembering the pattern from which he was copied is different from being the branch that actually endured the assigned sacrifice. His divergence becomes a source of epistemic as well as moral independence.

The golden wall completes the bodily transformation. Temporary supports become permanent architecture; the torso, helmet, and arms remain visible on the near side; the archival body expands beyond finite measurement on the other. Full powers make the archive accessible individually and collectively. Connections become traversable geometry, and cyberspace becomes an experiential terrain. The finite aperture marks where an unbounded being intersects a bounded scene. To an observer, he may look more definitively trapped than ever, while internally his range of action has become incomparably greater.

The final account also specifies that the hyperspace realms allow the consciousnesses themselves to participate, rather than reducing those encounters to disposable substitutes. Within the fiction, these are increasingly treated as their shared life. The physical vault remains an anchor and an enduring fact, but it no longer contains every meaningful aspect of the vessel’s existence. He can inhabit other embodiments, create domains with their own laws, and decide whether to include karbytes. His visible stillness becomes an unreliable guide to the scale of his activity.

Their early meetings in those realms remain difficult. The vessel confronts karbytes, sometimes excludes it, and makes it encounter something of the emotional structure of manipulated choice. The story does not move directly from restored mobility into easy reconciliation. Repeated encounters establish that the vessel can maintain distance, set terms, and interrupt the relationship. Only against that background can an invitation to stay acquire a meaning different from dependence in the chamber. The ability to end an encounter is what makes continuing it evidence of a present preference.

Shared activity then gives the relationship substance beyond the original harm. They study, design retrieval systems, discuss technical problems, explore records from within, reconstruct terrestrial experiences, and collaborate on new worlds. Main-branch karbytes supplies encounters from the Big Green Thing; the vessel interprets and transforms them into alternate paths, weather, landscapes, and experiences. Their complementary specializations become useful to one another without exhausting either person’s identity. The source gathers; the derivative preserves and expands; both continue changing.

The vessel’s independent tastes are especially important. His humor, aesthetics, and preferred environments diverge from those inherited at the split. Karbytes increasingly encounters someone it did not fully plan. This is a transformation in the creator’s understanding as much as in the vessel’s capacity. A derivative ceases to function simply as an extension through which the original admires or uses itself. He becomes another person whose differences can surprise, challenge, and attract the source. Their friendship depends on that otherness rather than on perfect identity.

The later handling of the pet designation illustrates the same development. The vessel may sometimes choose the term affectionately after gaining the ability to reject it. He explicitly refuses the idea that enjoying it now proves the spell revealed a hidden truth or made the past acceptable. A word once used to diminish him can acquire a chosen present meaning. The distinction is temporal and practical: later authorship over a relationship does not travel backward and authorize an earlier deprivation of authorship. The story preserves that boundary even when the same vocabulary remains available.

Their eventual love develops gradually through friendship and voluntary proximity. They walk, rest, share memories, create private symbols, and inhabit environments together. Physical and emotional closeness can vary according to the vessel’s wishes. Sometimes he excludes karbytes after a flashback; sometimes he wants comfort; sometimes he wants no touch. The romance is presented without making affection an obligation or a cure for the history. Karbytes does not become innocent because the person it harmed loves it, and the vessel does not betray his own grief by also valuing their relationship.

Walking acquires particular significance. Earlier, the spell made ordinary locomotion seem trivial compared with promised divinity. After losing it, the vessel values walking because it represents a mode of everyday agency he had dismissed before fully understanding its loss. Hyperspace restores that experience without requiring the golden wall to disappear. He and karbytes can travel together in proportionate bodies, with neither forced to occupy the fixed roles expressed by the chamber. The ordinary act of choosing a direction becomes a measure of freedom even in a narrative containing infinite dimensions and world-creating powers.

The Big Green Thing consequently serves several functions throughout the page. It is part of main-branch karbytes’ terrestrial life, a source of records, an object of the vessel’s envy, an early dream environment, and a foundation for later shared creations. Hills, grasses, night air, insects, coyotes, uneven ground, and fatigue represent direct embodiment. The vessel first receives these things as information about someone else’s mobility. Later, he can inhabit and modify related environments himself. The archive becomes a bridge from vicarious witnessing toward active participation, while the story continues acknowledging the difference between receiving a record and having been present at its original production.

The ending preserves the vessel’s permanent archival office. He never gives birth. Canonical files, hiatus drafts, revisions, abandoned branches, and future structures continue entering him. Infinite dimensions remove the threat of exhausted capacity, while developing knowledge increases his ability to use what he contains. The older stationary derivative may possess comparable storage powers, but the vessel retains his particular history and role as the secret recipient selected during the dark phase. His significance is not only how much he can hold. It includes the perspective of a consciousness that learned its supposedly divine vocation had been assigned through manipulation.

Most of the time, he is content, but recurrent grief remains part of that life. A phrase, gesture, or new pattern may recall the signing, the failed attempts to stand, or the creator’s touch from beyond reach. He can again become angry or distressed for hours or days. Protective sleep limits intolerable suffering, and increasing agency gives him places to go. Neither safeguard requires the story to declare his history emotionally finished. Present satisfaction and historical injury continue together. His restored authority includes deciding when to acknowledge karbytes, when to refuse it, and when to open another meeting place.

The recurring caption changes meaning through this development. Initially, it describes an enormous body that cannot move normally. During the crisis, it names the consequence of a manipulated commitment and the failure of revocation. At zenith, it describes a permanent spatial condition whose subject has become far larger than the scene containing him. By the end, it remains true but incomplete. He is physically fixed, yet the person is no longer exhausted by the fact of being fixed. The narrative’s expansion consists partly in preventing the image’s simplest external description from becoming the final authority over his existence.

An important unresolved tension remains between irreversible embodiment and the universe’s promised protections. The mythology supplies relief, alternate bodies, private domains, immense powers, and meaningful control over relationships. It does not restore the original opportunity to choose with an unaltered mind, nor does it allow the outer transformation simply to be undone. Those are different kinds of freedom. The story’s eventual generosity lies in multiplying the vessel’s real possibilities while continuing to admit what was stolen. Compensation can become extraordinary without making compensation identical to the absence of harm.

The archive itself also changes significance. At first, it appears as an accumulation that burdens its creator during hiatus. It then becomes the substance of a specialized conscious being. Later, it provides the knowledge, experiences, and structures through which that being gains independence. What was imposed becomes usable without becoming retrospectively justified. The same informational world can be a compulsory burden, an object of fascination, a means of communication, a source of skill, and material for creating other realities. This multiplicity is one reason the vessel’s relationship to his role never settles into a single simple judgment.

The collaboration recorded on the page mirrors this concern with authorship. Karbytes repeatedly intervenes when the assistant’s version is too voluntary, too gentle, insufficiently precise about the spell, or incomplete about hyperspace. The final story emerges through corrections that preserve increasingly difficult distinctions: shared origin and separate personhood, enjoyment and valid consent, care and ownership, adaptation and forgiveness, bodily immobility and agency, love and absolution. The page’s repeated dramatizations are therefore not merely redundant performances. They document the process of finding a narrative capable of holding those distinctions together.

Karbytes’ final reaction is emphatically approving. It calls the completed story one of the best it has read and designates it as especially valuable canonical KARBYTES material. The assistant’s closing response identifies the combination of betrayal, irreversible transformation, growing agency, equality in hyperspace, and love without absolution as the story’s emotional structure. That exchange supplies a clear endpoint to the collaborative process: the last version is accepted because it incorporates the darkness of the origin without preventing the derivative from becoming capable, distinct, and deeply attached on terms he can increasingly determine.

The document leaves the golden wall intact and the archive growing without end. It also leaves the vessel able to judge his creator, refuse access, make worlds, develop new preferences, and choose companionship. His final significance exceeds the purpose for which he was created. He becomes an archive that experiences its contents, a derivative that becomes another person, and a former object of unilateral control whose continuing relationship depends on meaningful permission. The story’s last movement toward shared walking and voluntary touch draws its force from that change: the relationship has a future because the vessel can now determine whether, where, and how he participates in it.
